content.text: ## Vans & Villains _Where's all the vanlife and travel stuff?_ At the dawn of 2026, my brother Skybreak and I started decoding beliefs and aspects of our lives and psyche that were not functioning... either that, or at least not correctly calibrated for our current reality. This surfaced the following conflicts and warring contradictions: * My favorite, purest, and longest lasting moments are 99% when I'm alone, recording nothing, just on the road and fully taking in a moment without any filter other than experience itself. * I tried to monetize my travels. * I want 3D recordings of my favorites to revisit them in virtual. I'm keeping the first one. It's the most crucial that I'd sacrifice everything for. Waking up and taking coffee in the back of the van while the morning mist rises through the fog that casts beams of light through the oak and Spanish moss. _Every moment matters._ The second, the YouTube channel, the Patreon, IG, etc. (and more than a decade of content) -- it's all being scrapped. Not scorched earth. I'll leave it online, but as abandoned... as hollow ruins. It's not worth sacrificing pure existence for them. Item 3: _The recordings and sharing with others?_ Those have been deprioritized and relegated to secondary experiences. If I go back to place, I'll look to capture that "second experience" to get those photos and videos. It's important to me. I've lost so many places like Mojo's Coffee House in Austin, The Oasis in Santa Fe, Art's Eatery in Durant... the list goes on. Capturing them in 3D remains a priority for the future in order to re-experience those places when afar, or worse, when lost to time and space. I'm still processing the impact, registering, digesting.. . but it _feels_ right. You'll still find many of my travel writings in "[Landlore](landlore)" -- yes, it's really happening, as well as the relics online: * [VAV on YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/@vansandvillains) * _"Your Road, Your Rules"_ as prints, stickers, and more [here on Redbubble](https://www.redbubble.com/shop/ap/37085735) * [OG Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/jayaprime/) * [OG Landlore Blogspot](https://landloreblog.blogspot.com/) PS: Duo Pocket, my current van, was stored away in Las Vegas when I left for Costa Rica in 2025. She's already been broken into once, and really I just hope they didn't damage her too much. Then I'm planning out a third van, Trinity, for here in a few years once back on the road on a more permanent basis. I'm also finally putting the finishing touches on my "[Bottle 66](bottle-66)" fictional travel story. So travel hasn't gone away. It's everywhere!

## Magic: the Gathering

_Where's all your MtG stuff!?!_

I've been playing the game ever since the original Antiquities set, ever since Chris Flemming turned to me in Chemistry class and asked me, "You wanna play a game?" The answer to that question _today_ is still the same as it was over 30-years ago. _Yes. FUCK YES!_

The book _"Apocalypse"_ was dedicated to me and my friend Dragontrainer by the smuggler himself, J Rob King (see image on right), and you could say I'm a little deep in the game. In my section on [WIPs and other writings](writing-wips), I go over some of the fanfic and future potential involvement.

I still play. These days I'm known for partnering different commanders with Yoshimaru, either that or with Rograkh, but I play literally every format of the game. My brother Skybreak and I might have a card or two that we could dust off.

While my now-infamous "Colors of Magic" fractal design is more rare these days, I still do special requests, with duffle bags, lunch boxes, and backpacks some of the most popular. [Contact me](contact). A few on-demand versions are still up for sale ([Redbubble](https://www.redbubble.com/shop/ap/182895224)) ([Threadless](https://fractals.threadless.com/designs/gathering-the-five-fractal-colors-of-magic/home/mini-art-print/framed-art-print)), but mostly I just do the fun custom stuff.

I've slowly been working on some designs for alternate art, especially custom sleeves and might start doing these more steadily. We'll see. I love how much we can express ourselves through the game, but... even more than that, even learn about ourselves, challenging myself to try styles that aren't native to my psyche. I took second place in the first ever MtG tourney to ever be held in Omaha, Nebraska, then dabbled in the pro-tour for a while. One of my favorite things these days is creating random-boards for commander decks to bring back variance and surprise to every game. . and. . I LOVE IT! Def my fav way to brew and rock out a deck! You'll find a few of those "expandable decks" on Archidekt ([link](https://archidekt.com/folders/627043)).

Look for MtG content to be added to this site in V4, launching 2027, July 31.

\[[Colors of Magic on Redbubble](https://www.redbubble.com/shop/ap/182895224)\]

## Photography

_Fractals are fine, but... where are all your photos?_

If you happened to breeze by that section on "Vans & Villains" above, let's just say I don't take many photos these days. NOT that I don't like it, and when I _do_ take photos, they fucking matter! I really could just blame it on Matthew Thomas, because ever since he painted a Sun 600 Polaroid for me, I've become more and more drawn to physical film. Then along came generative AI, the second wave, and combined with my own draw towards raw, non-recorded experience... . yeah, it was over.

I still take photos. They're rare. When I take a photo now, it means the world to me. I look at it over and over again. They're rarely far from me and every single one of them comes with a story. When Pocket was broken into a few months ago, it's funny, because one of the only things I hope they left behind was my camera. When I go up to see her in September, that's the first thing I'm checking after finding out if there's any damage.

I rarely share any of the polaroids online. BUT! If we happen to cross paths and you want to swap travel stories and experiences, then ask me about them. But this isn't a one-way door... I'll want your stories, too!

Until that moment, here are shots I took from Burning Man and mailed -- yes, snail mail, _I said it!_ -- to Matthew in thanks for the absolutely insane painting he did that turned my Polaroid camera into a living, breathing, work of art.

## The "Third Space" Quest

There IS still one place where you can still find me somewhat actively posting photos. With 428 photos and more than 24,000,000 views, I _do_ still post [here on Google Maps](https://www.google.com/maps/contrib/112121721953113641716). For example, that's where you'd find my photo here on the right from Fort Myers Public Library in Florida... among many, many others.

The quest I declared a decade ago remains the same. I am out to put every single public library and public park that I come across _en vrai_ onto Google Maps. That means photos, making sure location and details are correct, filling in missing information, and of course visiting the site. Now, more than ever, this "third space" where communities can arise are more important than ever. In fact, _fuck important!_ That shit doesn't describe it. _THIS is CRITICAL!_

I was already years deep into the quest when the pandemic hit. Coffee shops were part of the third space that got murdered.. . and still haven't recovered. Other gathering spaces were hit, with the underground itself nearly wiped out. I couldn't believe that even public parks were shut down for a few months in the pandemic. There's safety... and then there's straight denial of science.

So more than ever, I'm out to preserve these small parts that still exist. In fact, I still get "thank you" messages from librarians and likes on photos pretty much every week. Seriously, no thank you is needed. Libraries were my shelter during the decade that I lived on the streets. Even now, when traveling around by van, I stop in and soak up wifi while lounging amid the rows of books.

Even the nice librarian at Renton Library, when I was helping cleanup after the earthquake the day after Mardi Gras, she was so thankful and I'm like, "I was literally sleeping here just yesterday. Anytime you need me, just ask, 'cuz y'all are ALWAYS here for me!"

\[[My Photos on Google Maps](https://www.google.com/maps/contrib/112121721953113641716)\]

## Burn as One + The Art of Smoking

_Where's your pro-smoking art and activism at?_

Don't think for one single second that I've surrendered even an inch of my love for nicotine! Cigars, hookah, cigarettes, snorting lines of the brown devil itself, chaining vapes from one road trip to the next... look, if they made it readily available in needle form, I'd probably have more track-marks than just the two lovebites my right arm already carries. My absolute favorite brand has always been Djarum's original "Blacks" blend of kreteks.

But then came the summer of '09. That's when Obama signed "The Marlboro Monopoly Act" into law ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Family_Smoking_Prevention_and_Tobacco_Control_Act)). It was a targeted hit against every international form of nicotine, from my Indonesian kreteks to Indian bidis and beyond. Even the mainstream press -- who'd normally crucify tobacco for a cheap back-alley blowjob -- even _THEY_ were pointing out that the law was specifically engineered to secure a monopoly for legacy US tobacco companies.

So... I struck back.

I formed Burn as One, an organization dedicated solely to protecting art that featured tobacco. Just a few months later, I rallied more than a thousand artists and launched The Art of Smoking (aka, "TAOS") ([DeviantArt](https://www.deviantart.com/the-art-of-smoking/about)). Funny enough, my sister Faerie is still sitting right there as the icon at the very top of that group. That tyrannical law inadvertently brought us together from all corners of the globe. Since then, I've met so many incredible friends and collaborators across those groups -- including Helena, who fronts the art for "[The Passions of Blood, Smoke, and Oil](the-passions)", as well as Dez and Jaime who appear on the "[Warriors in Waiting](#?/warriors-in-waiting-live-set)" live set.

LiLi Glitch and I even spun up a Facebook page for TAOS, leaning heavily on LiLi to keep it running. She really held down the fort on that front, eventually calling me in as backup to help handle the death threats. Oh yeah, we had it all: attempted hack attacks on the main site, misguided morons flooding the group page, and, of course, the death threats. Honestly? The threats were always the fun part for me. I actually kinda miss it. I still maintain the site and the group today, but mostly just to protect them as sacred spaces.

Nowadays, I'm not even Stateside. Here in Costa Rica, the laws are a completely different beast. I can buy my kreteks locally, and they. are. _AMAZING!_ Easily one of the best blends you can find outside of Indonesia. So, while Burn as One and TAOS might not be heavily featured on the surface here, a massive chunk of the art I've made has been in direct collaboration with these incredible, cutthroat rebels who first found me through these groups.

\[[Burn as One dot Org](https://www.burnasone.org/)\] \[[#TAOS on DeviantArt](https://www.deviantart.com/the-art-of-smoking/about)\]

## Broken Gekko

_Where's all your code and dev stuff?_

The geckota dentata is about to be put to rest permanently. The main site itself is having the domain name nixed after two decades. I'm no longer selling my skills as a developer. Looking back in retrospect, I can say that my two favorite projects I ever worked on was for **Paper Street Flower Company** and for [**DharmaMix**](dharmamix). Both now defunct.

I still code and develop, but primarily vibe coding alongside Gemini 3.1 Pro inside of Google's Antigravity... and I don't do it for others. But I create apps all the time. If I'm looking for a solution on Google and need to click "Next Page", then I'm probably ceding and vibe coding my own app for it. I've got a whole Photoshop replacement, simple apps like image-doubling and collage grids, or even just an artist's mannequin that I can pose on the screen while making art.

I've saved the last surviving Broken Gekko page [here online](https://www.jayaprime.com/brokengekko/index.html).

Then you can find my growing collection of mini-apps <font color="#00f3ff">[here on the site](https://www.jayaprime.com/apps/index.html)</font>.

And instead of making sites and apps for others these days, I offer to take that same money and teach them to vibe code. Most of the students I've tutored in vibe coding have been at UNLV, but a few UT ATX rock stars are also in there. If you already have the exact concept in your mind -- and so clear 'n vivid that you can _see_ it -- and you've got the content (images, text, etc.) ready for launch, then [contact me](contact). We'll hype up on caffeine and get jiggy wid it!
